survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The provided excerpt does not include the underlying dataset documentation (e.g., which ILSA/LSA microdata file, cycle year, or whether complex survey weights were applied). For OECD/OECD-compiled large-scale evidence, analysts typically rely on sampling weights to produce population-representative estimates and may use replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife) for standard errors; however, this cannot be confirmed from the detected sections alone. If the report uses ILSA-style microdata, the appropriate weight variable would be the one supplied in the dataset (often a student/sampling weight such as W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT), and replicate weights would be used if variance estimation is described. If the report instead uses already-aggregated indicators or model outputs without microdata, weights may be inherently not applicable; the excerpt does not specify which case applies.
